speaker: Alex Chen
text: Thanks for joining today, Marcus. I'm Alex from NovaPay. I know you've been evaluating payment processors for FreshCart's expansion.

speaker: Marcus Webb
text: Yes, appreciate you making time. We're growing fast — 85 stores now, planning to hit 150 by year-end. Our current processor is getting expensive and the tools are outdated.

speaker: Alex Chen
text: Makes sense. Can I ask — who are you with currently and roughly what are you processing monthly?

speaker: Marcus Webb
text: We're on Fiserv, have been for about four years. We're doing around twelve million a month across all stores. Online is maybe fifteen percent of that.

speaker: Alex Chen
text: Twelve million monthly across 85 locations, with about 1.8 million online. That's solid volume. Let me walk you through how NovaPay handles that kind of scale.

speaker: Alex Chen
text: The core thing that sets us apart is our unified gateway. Right now, I'm guessing you have separate systems for in-store POS and ecommerce?

speaker: Marcus Webb
text: Exactly. Fiserv handles the terminals and we have a separate Stripe integration for the website. Reconciliation is a nightmare.

speaker: Alex Chen
text: That's a common setup and a common pain point. With NovaPay, both channels go through one API, one dashboard, one settlement file. Your finance team goes from juggling two reconciliation workflows down to one.

speaker: Marcus Webb
text: What does the pricing look like for our volume? We're paying about 2.7% blended right now and I know we can do better.

speaker: Alex Chen
text: We use interchange-plus pricing. For in-store, it's interchange plus 0.20% plus eight cents. For online, interchange plus 0.30% plus twelve cents. At your volume you'd qualify for our enterprise tier and volume discounts.

speaker: Marcus Webb
text: How does that compare in real terms? Like what's the all-in cost going to be?

speaker: Alex Chen
text: For a blended portfolio like yours — mostly card-present with some online — you'd land around 2.1% to 2.2% all-in for in-store and about 2.55% online. Compared to your current 2.7% blended, that's meaningful savings at twelve million a month.

speaker: Marcus Webb
text: That's interesting. What about chargebacks? We've been getting hit with a lot of disputes on the online side.

speaker: Alex Chen
text: Our chargeback fee is fifteen dollars, which gets waived if you win the dispute. But more importantly, we include our ShieldAI fraud detection engine. It's ML-based, trained on over two billion transactions. Typically reduces fraud losses by about 68%.

speaker: Marcus Webb
text: Is that included in the enterprise plan or is it extra?

speaker: Alex Chen
text: Full ShieldAI with custom ML models and custom rules is included on the enterprise plan. No extra charge per transaction. Stripe charges five cents per screened transaction for their equivalent, which adds up fast at your volume.

speaker: Marcus Webb
text: Good. Now, here's a big question for us. We're looking at expanding into Canada next year and possibly the UK the year after. Can NovaPay handle multi-currency transactions?

speaker: Alex Chen
text: Great question. So right now NovaPay processes in USD only. We have confirmed expansion to Canada and the UK planned for Q3 2026. Multi-currency settlement is on the roadmap but I want to be upfront — it's not available today.

speaker: Marcus Webb
text: That's a concern. Our Canadian stores would need to accept Canadian dollars. What would the interim solution look like?

speaker: Alex Chen
text: For the interim, the typical approach is to use NovaPay for your US operations and a separate processor like Stripe for Canada, then consolidate once we launch there. It's not ideal but it means you get the savings domestically right away.

speaker: Marcus Webb
text: Hmm. What about data security? We went through a PCI audit last year and it was painful. What certifications do you hold?

speaker: Alex Chen
text: We're PCI DSS Level 1 certified, the highest level. Also SOC 2 Type II. All card data is tokenized at entry — raw numbers never hit your servers if you use our hosted checkout or drop-in SDK. That keeps you at SAQ-A, the simplest PCI tier.

speaker: Marcus Webb
text: That would be a huge improvement. Our current setup requires us to maintain full PCI compliance because we handle the card data ourselves.

speaker: Alex Chen
text: Exactly, and that's expensive to maintain. With our SDK approach, the compliance burden drops dramatically. You'd go from PCI DSS Level 1 requirements down to SAQ-A, which is a 20-question self-assessment instead of a full audit.

speaker: Marcus Webb
text: How long does a typical integration take for a retailer our size? We have 85 locations on Verifone terminals plus the ecommerce site.

speaker: Alex Chen
text: We work with Verifone, so that's good. For a full rollout — terminals plus ecommerce — we typically see four to six weeks. Our solutions team handles the migration. On the enterprise plan, migration support is included at no cost.

speaker: Marcus Webb
text: What about our loyalty program? We have a custom loyalty system that hooks into the payment flow to award points at checkout. Would that still work?

speaker: Alex Chen
text: It should, but I'd want our solutions team to review the integration. Our API supports metadata fields on each transaction — up to 20 key-value pairs. Most loyalty integrations use that to pass the member ID and point calculation. Let me set up a technical call for that.

speaker: Marcus Webb
text: Okay. And one more thing — what kind of uptime guarantees do you offer? We can't have our POS terminals going down during peak hours.

speaker: Alex Chen
text: Enterprise plan includes a 99.99% uptime SLA. We run active-active across two AWS regions. In the last 12 months we've had zero outages. Our status page is public if you want to verify that.

speaker: Marcus Webb
text: Alright, I think I have a good picture. Let me summarize where I'm at. The pricing is compelling, the fraud detection is a big plus, and the PCI simplification would save us a lot of headaches. The Canada thing is the one sticking point.

speaker: Alex Chen
text: Totally fair. How about this — I'll put together a formal proposal with projected savings based on your twelve million monthly volume. And I'll get you a firm timeline from our product team on the Canada launch. Can we schedule a follow-up next Thursday?

speaker: Marcus Webb
text: Thursday works. Also, can you send over the API documentation? My CTO will want to review the technical side before the next call.

speaker: Alex Chen
text: Absolutely. I'll send the API docs, the security whitepaper, and sandbox credentials so your team can start playing with the integration. Anything else you need from us?

speaker: Marcus Webb
text: No, I think that covers it. Thanks Alex, talk Thursday.

speaker: Alex Chen
text: Thanks Marcus. Looking forward to it.
